verdict.rationale: Elastic documents alerting rules at the service, environment, and transaction level and through custom KQL queries. It also documents log-threshold alerts and sending notifications to services or third-party incident management systems, which covers the alerting and basic notification core. The evidence says nothing about notification grouping or silencing, and routing is only implied by the mention of notification destinations. missing for 10: notification grouping/deduplication, silencing/snoozing/maintenance windows, explicit routing rules per alert, evidence of alerting on every signal type (metrics, traces, synthetics), independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an SRE, I can alert on any telemetry signal with routing, grouping, and silencing of notifications

citations.quote: You can define rules at different levels (service, environment, transaction) or use custom KQL queries.
You can also extend your alerts with notifications via services or third-party incident management systems.
You can create a rule to send an alert when the log aggregation exceeds a threshold.
